Question B-006-007-004.

Why the correct answer is right: A half-wave antenna’s electric field follows the element orientation, so an element perpendicular to the Earth’s surface produces vertical polarization.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Circular": Circular polarization needs two orthogonal components in phase quadrature; a single straight half-wave element mounted vertically does not create that field.
- sourceIndex 2: "Horizontal": Horizontal polarization would come from a half-wave element mounted parallel to the Earth’s surface, not perpendicular to it.
- sourceIndex 3: "Elliptical": Elliptical polarization is not produced merely by making a single half-wave radiator vertical; it requires mixed components with unequal amplitudes or phases.
